items.title: ISIS-linked families to arrive in Australia today after years in Syria
items.description: Australian authorities are preparing for the arrival of 13 women and children linked to Islamic State fighters. As some of the women were boarding their flight, they told the ABC they were excited to get back to Australia despite the AFP warning some might face arrest.

items.title: Live: Israel strikes Beirut for first time since Hezbollah ceasefire
items.description: The strikes come as Iran weighs up a peace deal put forward by the US, with Donald Trump saying the war could "be at an end". Follow live.

items.title: Iran reviews US proposal as Trump says war could 'be at an end'
items.description: Iran reviews a new peace-deal proposal from the US, which President Donald Trump says could end the war, but an Iranian official describes it as an "American wish list".

items.title: Albanese's budget won't be derailed by Trump's pronouncements
items.description: It's clear that whatever this unpredictable US president says, the Albanese government isn't expecting a return to normal oil flows any time soon.

items.title: Is Richard Dawkins right about AI?
items.description: Is AI conscious? Richard Dawkins is asking the wrong question.

items.title: This island was once ruled by Australia. Now, it could become the world's newest country
items.description: A tropical archipelago just 1,500 kilometres from Australia is readying to become the world's newest country. But as Bougainville nears independence, memories of a bloody past are coming back to the surface.

items.title: 'I'll show no mercy': Charity founder faces 'tickle torture' allegations
items.description: More victims of former Order of Australia recipient Cody Schaeffer have spoken to the ABC about his actions.

items.title: Leader who overcame One Nation's rise warns against dismissing its voters
items.description: Nearly three decades after One Nation's shock breakthrough in Queensland, Pauline Hanson's party is again within reach of a significant political victory.

items.title: What if we used taxes or superannuation to control inflation, not interest rates?
items.description: As the average mortgage borrower confronts another $100 a month on top of their already inflated repayments, lots of people are asking if there is a better way to contain inflation than simply raising interest rates. It turns out there might be.

items.title: The generation gap is real, but the 'bank of mum and dad' complicates it
items.description: Next week's budget will have the generation gap at its heart. But nailing down exactly what that gap is can be difficult. Here's what the evidence says.

items.title: One answer to Australia's housing affordability crisis is hidden in plain sight
items.description: What if the sudden improvement in Iain's life, and the extra $600 a month in his pocket, can be traced back to a single policy decision made by a federal minister in the 1980s?

items.title: Canary Islands leader does not want hantavirus-hit cruise ship to dock
items.description: A luxury cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak and marooned for days off the coast of Cape Verde with close to 150 people on board is on its way to Spain's Canary Islands, where a regional leader says it is not welcome.

items.title: What will become of the Victoria Barracks? Communities have their say
items.description: Veteran, housing, heritage and community organisations are urging the government to put public needs first as dozens of defence sites get prepped for sale.

items.title: Ted Turner, pioneering founder of CNN, dead at 87
items.description: Turner revolutionised television news when he launched the world's first 24-hour news channel in 1980.

items.title: Exit 8 explores the mundane horror of life in a loop
items.description: The creator of the minimalist horror film hopes it inspires viewers to stop doomscrolling and take a look at the world around them.

items.title: Can you identify Aussie movies from a single frame?
items.description: Think you know your Moulin Rouge from your Muriel's Wedding? Take our Australian movie quiz to prove you're the king of The Castle.

items.title: Explore Australia with these five great road trips
items.description: Whether you want to explore the red desert or picnic by a waterfall, an Aussie road trip awaits.

items.title: Paddock-to-plate revival as farmers grapple with surging food freight costs
items.description: As the cost of each kilometre food travels explodes, growers and consumers are looking for ways to shorten the supply chain.

items.title: Children in Melbourne's inner west at higher risk of asthma hospital visits
items.description: There are renewed calls for government action after another study finds children in Melbourne's inner west are over-represented in asthma-related hospital visits.

items.title: NSW gun industry calls for buyback to be scrapped amid plummeting sales
items.description: Gun sales are plummeting across NSW, with the industry calling for a proposed buyback to be scrapped. But a public health expert says safety must take priority over retail concerns.

items.title: One Nation corflutes backing Ben Roberts-Smith spark legal warning
items.description: One Nation election advertising stating the party's support for Ben Roberts-Smith, who is charged with carrying out war crimes in Afghanistan, has legal experts worried.

items.title: Mother's warning after cake-decorating dust leaves toddler in coma
items.description: The mother of a Queensland toddler who is in an induced coma after inhaling a dust used for decorating cakes is calling for similar products to be pulled from shelves.

items.title: Child protection workers stood down over Kumanjayi Little Baby
items.description: Three child protection workers have been stood down and a department-wide review ordered over its handling of Kumanjayi Little Baby's circumstances before her alleged murder.

items.title: Pussy Riot joins anti-Russia smoke bomb protest at Venice Biennale
items.description: Among those in the crowed were members of the Russian punk group Pussy Riot, who attended protests against the country's participation in the Italian art show.

items.title: Cancellation 'disaster' for business that expected Inland Rail for 25 years
items.description: Regional communities from Queensland to Victoria react after the major federal rail project was axed overnight.
